# UFO Feel — Intake brief (final, producer answers incorporated)

**FINAL DRAFT** — producer answered Q1=B, Q2=C, Q3=A (see Appendix).
Stage to follow: intake_complete (via intake finish + coverage review).

## Problem statement

The Mystery UFO collector drone flies, harvests and dies **silently and
without feedback**: it has no visual effects and no sounds for any lifecycle
moment, so the reward reads as dead game feel. We need the classic Space
Invaders mystery-ship juice: a "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble while it is deployed,
a reward cue when it returns to the player, and an explosion plus a "tinkle" of
dropped resources when it is destroyed — with full-juice VFX at every lifecycle
stage.

## Users

- **Player** (the primary stakeholder) — wants the Mystery UFO to *feel* like
  the Space Invaders homage it is: an audible, celebratory arcade reward with
  visible juice at spawn, on collect, on return and on death.
- **Developer / quality gates** — wants the juice to run through the existing
  ToneForge audio pipeline and shared VFX so the game and every gym stay
  identical (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear the classic UFO warble for the drone's whole
  sortie so I always know it is out there farming for me.
- As a player, I want to see the saucer come alive (running-light pulse, a poof
  on launch, sparkles as it vacuums, a trail on the way home) so the drone
  reads as a living reward.
- As a player, I want a reward fanfare when the drone flies home and pays out
  so the economic payoff feels earned.
- As a player, I want a satisfying explosion and the tinkle of minerals
  scattering when an enemy shoots the drone down, so the loss/opportunity
  reads clearly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Warble loop (Q2=C).** A classic "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble cue plays continuously from spawn through the **seek and collect** phases (the whole sortie) and stops when the drone begins its return leg, pays out, is destroyed, or is torn down — delivered as a start/stop continuous cue with control companions (mirroring `stopDiveSound`/`stopThrusterSound`), at a level-appropriate audible gain that respects the shared SFX volume/mute settings.
2. **Reward cue (Q3=A).** A distinct reward fanfare plays on **arrival at the player**, synchronised with the hold pay-in (exactly when `MysteryUfoDrone._payOut` credits the sink), so the payout moment is audible.
3. **Destruction feedback.** On enemy destruction the drone plays an explosion cue **and** spawns the explosion particle VFX at the crash site (reusing `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`); a mineral "tinkle" cue fires in sync with the spilled resource drops (spill already exists via `hitDrone`/`scatterMineralDrops`), so the dropped minerals read audibly.
4. **Full-juice VFX (Q1=B).** Code-drawn Phaser graphics (no external art) add the full lifecycle juice: spawn poof at launch, per-mineral collect sparkle/ring while vacuuming, a running-light pulse animation on the saucer rim, and a return-leg trail/glow — all in addition to the destruction explosion VFX.
5. **Pipeline, parity & quality.** Every new cue is a baked ToneForge delivery (recipe YAMLs under `audio/toneforge/recipes/`, entries in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, wrappers in `src/audio/effects.ts`, WAVs rendered via `npm run build-audio`); the cue-manifest / effects-contract / build-audio / audio-balance-guard suites pass; the continuous warble has start/stop control lifecycle and every cue degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext; the VFX/SFX run through shared core so `PlayScene` and the gym scenes are identical (duplicate-body guard + gym-parity docs assertion pass, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` green); the full project test suite passes and relevant docs (GDD §7.3 / Mystery UFO section, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`) are updated.

## Constraints

- Audio must flow through the existing ToneForge pipeline — no new external
  assets (procedural WAV baked at build time; `file:../ToneForge` dependency).
- The continuous warble requires start/stop control lifecycle (`ControlCues` in
  the manifest) and must respect the shared SFX volume/mute settings.
- VFX must be code-drawn Phaser graphics (repo convention: no external art).
- Every cue must be a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests and
  autoplay-blocked browsers) — the effects contract suite enforces this.
- Behaviour must live once in shared core (`src/scenes/core/`) and be consumed
  by both the game and the gyms (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).
- Peak-volume/balance guarded by `scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs`.

## Existing state

- `MysteryUfoDrone` (src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts) is a pure entity with a
  code-drawn saucer (running lights, dome, glow) but **zero VFX/SFX**: no cue is
  called anywhere in the drone, the shared pass (`src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts`),
  or the spawn path. Collection (`_vacuum`) hides minerals with no feedback;
  destruction (`_destroyByEnemy` + `hitDrone`) already spills minerals via
  `scatterMineralDrops` but with no explosion/tinkle feedback.
- The audio pipeline is ToneForge-baked: `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` maps
  every cue to a recipe; `src/audio/effects.ts` exports thin playback wrappers;
  WAVs are baked by `npm run build-audio`. No UFO cue exists yet.

## Desired change

Add the "feel" layer so every Mystery UFO lifecycle moment gives feedback
through the shared pipeline, identically in the game and the gyms: warble for
the whole sortie, a reward fanfare on payout, explosion + mineral tinkle +
particle burst on destruction, plus the full-juice VFX set (spawn poof, collect
sparkle, running-light pulse, return trail).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts` — lifecycle state hooks (spawn, collect,
  return, payout, destroyed) driving the SFX/VFX seams; running-light pulse
  animation in the saucer draw/update.
- `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` — shared tick/spawn/destroy pass: warble
  start/stop in `tickDrones`, destruction explosion + tinkle adjacent to the
  existing spill in `hitDrone`, spawn poof in `spawnDrone`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` /
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — shared wiring so game and gyms run the same code.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new cue wrappers: warble loop + `stopMysteryUfoWarbleSound`
  control companion, `playMysteryUfoRewardSound`, `playMysteryUfoDestroySound`,
  `playMineralTinkleSound`.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new cue→recipe entries (+ control cue).
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/*.yaml` — new `aihell-mystery-ufo-*` recipes
  (warble, reward, destroy, mineral tinkle).
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` / `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts` / `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts`
  — continuous-cue start/stop plumbing for the warble.
- `src/vfx/` — spawn poof, collect sparkle/ring, return trail (small new/module
  effects, following `explosionParticles.ts` conventions); `explosionParticles.ts`
  reused for the destruction burst.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§7.3 + Mystery UFO section),
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV9G113S009B37I** — Mystery UFO has no visible representation (epic,
  completed): the collector-drone entity and shared pass this item adds feel to.
- **AH-0MVH7ZC5N003JS92** — Mystery UFO needs a better graphical representation
  (completed): the code-drawn saucer VFX baseline this item animates.
- **AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7** — Space Invaders mystery UFO bonus (completed): the
  classic reference the warble/reward homage draws from.
- **AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J** — Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to
  ToneForge (epic): the pipeline every new cue must flow through.
- **AH-0MVBMPZ2C0008VAE** — Drone level variables and curve specs (completed).
- **AH-0MVBMQ0HR0064THH** — Gym parity for the collector drone (completed).

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: **VFX scope.** "The item says the Mystery UFO currently has no VFX or
  SFX but does not specify which visual effects to add. (a) Minimal...; (b)
  Full juice — also add spawn poof, return-trail/glow, running-light pulse;
  (c) Sound-only."
  — Answer (producer, via review reply "1. B (with SFX)"): **B — full juice**,
  with the SFX set confirmed in scope alongside the VFX. Source: producer
  review reply on AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6 (comment thread
  AH-C0MVNZ64M5000W4NL). Final AC 4 (full-juice VFX) + ACs 1–3 (SFX) reflect
  this.
- Q2: **"woo-woo-woo" delivery.** "(a) continuous looping cue while the drone
  is in the collect phase; (b) discrete one-shot per collected mineral; (c) a
  looping cue that plays for the whole sortie (seek+collect)."
  — Answer (producer, "2. C"): **C — loop for the whole sortie** (seek +
  collect), so the warble starts at spawn and ends at return/payout/destruction.
  Source: producer review reply. Final AC 1 reflects this.
- Q3: **Reward timing.** "(a) on arrival at the ship, synchronised with the
  payout pay-in; (b) when the drone begins the return leg; (c) both."
  — Answer (producer, "3. A"): **A — on arrival/payout**, synced with the hold
  credit. Source: producer review reply. Final AC 2 reflects this.

### Assumptions (documented)

- The original description's "no VFX or VFX" is a typo for "no VFX or SFX"
  (confirmed implicitly by Q1 answer B *with SFX*).
- Level progression (lifetime/capacity/radius) does **not** change the sound
  character — same cues at every level (no per-level variant recipes).
- New cues respect the existing volume balance budget (≤ ~0.2 peak per layer,
  `audio-balance-guard`) and the global SFX mute/volume settings automatically
  via the shared playback provider.
- Running-light pulse is a static-free animation of the existing
  code-drawn lights (alpha/colour oscillation), not a new emitter.

### Risks

- **Audio-pipeline risk (med).** Every new cue is a build-time WAV bake: recipe
  YAML, manifest entry, wrapper and `npm run build-audio` render must stay in
  lock-step or the contract suites (cue-manifest / effects-contract /
  build-audio / audio-balance-guard) fail red. Mitigation: follow the exact
  pattern of an existing baked cue (e.g. `aihell-diver-dive-loop`) end to end.
- **Continuous-cue lifecycle risk (med).** The sortie-long warble must start
  exactly once at spawn and stop on every terminal path (return, payout,
  destroyed, teardown) or it will leak a looping voice. Mitigation: start/stop
  via the shared control-companion pattern (`ControlCues`) and asset in
  `tickDrones` where removal is final; extend the cue-contract test to assert
  stop-on-all-terminals.
- **Collect-sparkle VFX performance (low-med).** At the max collector radius
  (40 px) a drone can vacuum several minerals in one tick; a sparkle per
  mineral must be small, short-lived and capped, not an unbounded emitter.
  Mitigation: reuse `explosionParticles`-style pooled graphics and cap per-tick
  spawns.
- **Parity risk (med).** If a gym or `PlayScene` wires the SFX/VFX outside the
  shared core, the duplicate-body guard / gym-parity docs assertion fail and
  the game and gyms drift. Mitigation: implement through
  `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` and shared hooks only (AGENTS.md
  architecture convention).
- **Scope-creep risk (med).** The chosen full-juice VFX set (poof, sparkle,
  pulse, trail) is wide for one item. Extra polish discovered during
  implementation (e.g. pay-in burst on the ship, level-scaled bloom) must be
  recorded as new work items, not absorbed into this one.

### Duplicate-work check

Performed `wl search "UFO"` / `"woo"` / `"mystery ufo vfx"` — completed items
cover visual representation (AH-0MVH7ZC5N003JS92), visibility epic
(AH-0MV9G113S009B37I) and the classic reference (AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7); **no
overlapping item for UFO audio/VFX feel exists**. No duplicate — proceed.
---

## Plan: changelog (plan skill, AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6)

- **2026-10-28** — Planned via /skill:plan. Pre-check `plan-if-needed` → `plan` (Small/Medium); plan-approval-gate → `request_approval: false` (no approval pause). Created 6 child items (test-first): UFO feel test seams, ToneForge UFO cue bake, Sortie warble lifecycle, Terminal reward and destruction feedback, Saucer lifecycle VFX juice, UFO feel docs and quality gate. Deps wired (test seams + cue bake → warble → terminal feedback; VFX → docs/gate). Parent AC section unwrapped to single lines so AC coverage is machine-comparable (formatting only). Six automated review stages run; AC coverage review → `proceed` (all 5 parent ACs covered). Parent stage → `plan_complete`. Effort/risk reused from existing estimate (Small / Medium, comment AH-C0MVNZHO3W000ZBLP) — not re-estimated.

### Appendix addition (planning run)

- Q: "Did planning need any further clarifying questions from the producer?" — Answer (this run): No new questions. All three design decisions were already resolved in intake (Q1=B full juice, Q2=C whole-sortie warble, Q3=A arrival/payout, recorded above), the effort/risk estimate is on file, and the plan-approval gate requested no approval. Planning proceeded from the intake brief's Acceptance Criteria directly.

# Intake Brief — Waves need more variation in enemy types

**Headline:** Make all 100 campaign waves draw from a wider enemy-type mix so no two sequential waves share the same enemy composition, while preserving each level's dominant-archetype identity and the existing difficulty ramp, fire boundary and determinism contract.

## Seed description

> Waves within a level should show more variation in enemy types.

## Problem statement

The shipped 10 × 10 campaign (100 waves) reads as repetitive within each level: Level 1 is Scout-only across all ten waves, Level 5 is Phaser-only, and the `fixed` filler waves in Levels 1–3 and the `fixed` showcases throughout are hand-authored compositions reused verbatim. Only L1W1, L1W2, L2W1 and L2W2 are `dynamic`. Within-level enemy-type variety is therefore the exception rather than the rule, and a player experiences long runs of the same enemies (e.g. ten Scout waves in a row at the start of the run).

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, I want each wave in a level to field different enemy types from the preceding wave, so the campaign feels varied rather than monotonous across a run.
- **As a player**, I want each level to keep a recognisable identity (its dominant archetype), so the onboarding ramp and the "Predictable Death" pattern-testing level stay legible.
- **As a designer**, I want the variation enforced as a campaign-wide invariant (not per-level hand-tuning), so future wave edits cannot silently reintroduce sequential repetition.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No sequential repetition.** No two sequential waves anywhere in the built campaign (Levels 1–10 × 10 waves, `buildSequencedLevels()` output) share the same enemy composition. *Verification:* unit/integration test asserting pairwise distinctness of adjacent waves across all 100 waves at default config; applies to `curve`, `dynamic` and `fixed` modes alike.
- **AC2 — Whole-campaign coverage.** All 100 waves are in scope (not just the opening four); every level's wave list shows more than one enemy archetype across its ten waves. *Verification:* per-level archetype-count assertion ≥ 2 across the ten waves.
- **AC3 — Level identity preserved.** Each level keeps its dominant archetype identity (Level 1 Scout-dominant, Level 5 Phaser-dominant; classic-arcade levels keep their showcase archetypes), varying *around* it with secondary archetypes. *Verification:* per-level dominant-archetype assertions; GDD §3.2 identity text still holds.
- **AC4 — Balance rules respected.** Generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves continue to satisfy the classification balance rules R1–R3 (opening formation-only, no all-chaser wave, bounded ranged mix). *Verification:* existing `waveBalance` audit/validator tests still pass over the rebuilt campaign.
- **AC5 — No regression of difficulty ramp and boundaries.** The non-decreasing target difficulty, the Levels 1–3 no-fire / Levels 4–10 fire boundary, and the wave-10 mini-boss encounters are unchanged; the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins pass. *Verification:* existing campaign regression and invariant suites.
- **AC6 — Determinism and reproducibility.** Same seed reproduces the same campaign; `curve`/`fixed` waves stay seed-independent, `dynamic` waves remain a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed). *Verification:* seeded-build equality tests as in the opening-variety item (AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B).
- **AC7 — Testing/validation.** New or updated unit/integration tests cover sequential distinctness, per-level identity, determinism and regression; **the full project test suite passes with the new changes**.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated, including code comments, `README.md`, the GDD (§3.2 level descriptions and the default-campaign note), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and any relevant docs-site entries.

## Constraints

- **Existing archetypes only** (consistent with AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B): re-mix the 18-archetype roster (`scout`, `diver`, `tank`, `phaser`, `swarm`, `boss`, `asteroid`, `harvester`, `march`, `capturer`, `ghost-chase`, `ghost-ambush`, `ghost-flank`, `ghost-wander`, `grunt`, `raider`, `lane-traffic`, `orbital-strike`); do not invent new archetypes unless the producer explicitly requests them.
- **"Same enemies"** is interpreted as the same set of enemy archetypes in a wave's composition (order/spacing/count variations alone are not "different enemies"). The sequential-distinctness rule applies to generated waves as well (producer Q3 = c').
- **Level identity (Q2 = a):** the dominant archetype of each level is preserved; variety is added around it.
- **Mixed mechanism (Q3 = c'):** hand-authored `fixed` waves stay where a specific showcase/pin is required (wave-10 mini-bosses, classic-arcade debuts, L1 onboarding pin); `curve` waves stay deterministic; filler waves that are currently `fixed` may move to `dynamic` where safe, seeded per-run under R1–R3 guardrails.
- **Determinism contract** (AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT): `curve`/`fixed` seed-independent; `dynamic` pure function of (curve, pool, seed).
- **Fire boundary** (GDD §2.4/§2.5): Levels 1–3 do not fire; Levels 4–10 do. Generated waves derive fire rules from level number.
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): wave data/logic live in the shared core consumed by both `PlayScene` and the gyms; any divergence must be justified and recorded.
- **No target-curve re-tuning unless required** to satisfy AC1–AC3; if the ramp must move to break sequential repetition, it stays within the no-degeneracy + non-decreasing + strictly-rising aggregated difficulty constraints.
- **UK English** in all code comments, tests and documentation.

## Existing state

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — 100 rows; L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2 `dynamic`; most other L1–L3 rows `fixed`; L5W2 `dynamic`; Level 4+ mixed `curve`/`fixed`; wave 10 of every level `fixed` mini-boss.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS` hand-authored waves (used for `fixed`); Level 1 all Scout V-formations; Level 5 Phaser-only; classic-arcade showcases on Levels 6–10.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_FIXED_LEVELS`, `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES`, `defaultDifficultyCurves()`; per-wave mode overrides supported (`DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES[level]?.[wave]`).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — per-wave `generation` dispatch (`curve`/`fixed`/`dynamic`); `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION` for openings; seeded dynamic jitter.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — runtime auto-sequencer; `defaultCandidatePool()`; composition from `enemyDifficulty` targets.
- `src/core/waveBalance.ts` — pure R1–R3 rules + validator (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP); generator hard-constraints.
- Tests: `waveBalance.test.ts`, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`, `campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `sequencedLevels.test.ts` (incl. "Retuned default campaign (AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K)" and phaser-only filler pins), `WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 (L1 Scout V-formations).

## Desired change

- Extend enemy-type variety across all 100 waves so sequential waves differ in composition, per level identity (Q2 = a) and via the mixed fixed/curve/dynamic mechanism (Q3 = c').
- Introduce a campaign-wide sequential-distinctness invariant (producer Q1 = a + explicit rule), enforced in the shared builder/sequencer and tested.
- Keep hand-authored `fixed` waves where showcase/pin/identity requires; relax only what is needed to satisfy AC1–AC2.
- Where safe, convert currently-`fixed` filler waves to `dynamic` (seeded per-run variety) under the balance-rule guardrails; otherwise extend the authored `LEVELS` data to mix secondary archetypes into identity waves.
- Update documentation (GDD §3.2 level wording, default-campaign note, enemy-design docs, README, code comments).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — per-wave `generation` mode changes; possible minor target retunes for AC1–AC2.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — add secondary archetypes to identity-preserving `fixed` waves; keep showcases/mini-bosses.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — sequential-distinctness enforcement seam; possibly broaden `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION`-style curation to filler waves.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — composition constraint for sequential distinctness if enforced in the sequencer; pool/jitter tuning.
- `src/core/waveBalance.ts` — reuse R1–R3 validator for sequential-distinctness auditing (additive rule/named constant if needed).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES` updates if filler waves move to `dynamic`.
- Tests — `sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `campaignInvariants.test.ts` (or new `campaignVariety.test.ts`), `WaveManager.test.ts`, `configStore.test.ts`, `csv-seed.test.ts`.
- Docs — `docs/Game Design Document.md` §3.2 + default-campaign note, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B** — Create more variety in the first 3-4 waves (completed v0.1.9): made L1W1..L2W2 `dynamic`; the partial-overlap precedent this item extends to all 100 waves.
- **AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP** — Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling (completed v0.1.13): R1–R3 rules + validator; must keep passing (AC4).
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** — Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign (completed): the ramp/regression pins AC5 preserves.
- **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT** — Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration (completed): the mode dispatch + determinism contract.
- **AH-0MVCYANT6003SG5C / AH-0MVCRAR89009C8GZ** — 10-wave campaign data foundation + re-land (completed v0.1.14): the 100-wave grid this item varies.
- **AH-0MV398ZWL009TTOB** — Write campaign-level invariant tests (completed): precedent for campaign-wide invariants.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — identity vs sequential-distinctness tension (high).** Level 1 (Scout) and Level 5 (Phaser) must keep a dominant archetype yet not repeat across ten waves. *Mitigation:* allow 2–3 archetypes per level with the dominant sharing the most waves; assert "≥ 2 archetypes per level" plus "no adjacent identical composition", not "all ten waves distinct types".
- **Risk — ramp/regression disturbance (medium).** Re-mixing archetypes can shift `targetDifficulty` fit. *Mitigation:* reuse the retuned targets; retune only within the no-degeneracy/non-decreasing/strictly-rising constraints if required; keep the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K pins green.
- **Risk — sequencer target misses under a distinctness constraint (medium).** Enforcing "different archetype set from the previous wave" in `curve`/`dynamic` generation can push some waves off their `targetDifficulty` or shrink the candidate space. *Mitigation:* bias the sequencer towards the previous wave's complement (rules may trade exact target match for distinctness, following the R1–R3 precedence in AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP), or hand-author that wave as `fixed`; record resulting target error in the balance audit.
- **Risk — scope creep.** New archetypes, per-wave special mechanics, or reworking mini-bosses are out of scope; record as linked work items.
- **Assumption — existing archetypes only** (consistent with AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B); no new archetypes unless the producer requests them.
- **Assumption — "same enemies" = same archetype set** in a wave's composition; count/order/spacing changes do not count as distinct.
- **Assumption — Q3 = c'** reads as the recommended mixed mechanism (authored `fixed` where pinned; `dynamic` for filler where safe), with the sequential-distinctness rule binding on generated waves too. If the producer intended otherwise, the mechanism sections of this brief change but AC1–AC3, AC5–AC8 stand.
- **Assumption — the sequential-distinctness rule is cross-wave, not cross-level** ("sequential within a level"); a wave-10 mini-boss and the next level's wave 1 are different levels and are not compared.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope — which waves need more enemy-type variation?" — Answer (producer, AH-C0MVNZ88SK007XAFJ): **(a)** all 100 campaign waves, **plus the explicit rule: no two sequential waves should have the same enemies**. Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q2: "Level identities — should the deliberate single-type levels stay pure?" — Answer (producer, AH-C0MVNZ8CBE00748J3): **(a)** preserve each level's dominant archetype/identity but add variety around it. Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q3: "Mechanism — deterministic authored waves or seeded dynamic per-run variation?" — Answer (producer, AH-C0MVNZ8FVZ005AERQ): **(c')** mixed, as in the recommended (c); the sequential-distinctness constraint applies to generated waves too. Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Research (agent): current campaign state audited (10 × 10 grid, mode ledger per wave); Level 1 Scout-only and Level 5 Phaser-only identities pinned by GDD §3.2/§2.5 and by `WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 / `sequencedLevels.test.ts` phaser-only pins; duplicate check performed (partial overlap only with AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B). Source: repo inspection + worklog search, this session (comments AH-C0MVNZ7UJ1005DJ9V).

## Related work (automated report)

_Appended after the find-related skill run (step 7)._

## Plan: feature decomposition

Decomposed into nine child work items following a **test-first, three-phase vertical-slice** cadence. Each phase cuts through data, code, tests and comments; the next phase's item descriptions are reviewed after each phase lands.

### Phase A — measure, then pilot the hardest case

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Campaign variety audit + failing invariants (AH-0MVSE6D2L0034SKG) | feature | Shared pure module `waveComposition` / `auditCampaignVariety` / `LEVEL_IDENTITY` + staged campaign assertions and the red-baseline audit snapshot |
| A2 | Relax single-type pins to identity-preserving (AH-0MVSE6F0O00689TT) | task | Convert "scouts only" / "phasers only" pins into dominance assertions (Q2=a) |
| A3 | Level 1 + Level 5 pilot: identity-preserving variety (AH-0MVSE6VIW009QG2E) | feature | Tracer bullet on the two highest-risk identity levels |

### Phase B — enforce, then rework the campaign

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Enforce sequential distinctness for generated waves (AH-0MVSE6XIO007BXYM) | feature | Seeded-deterministic constraint on `curve`/`dynamic` waves, R1–R3 precedence preserved |
| B2 | Authored variety rework — Levels 2–4 (onboarding) (AH-0MVSE7F090010EG3) | feature | Re-mix the no-fire onboarding `fixed` waves |

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Campaign variety regression, determinism and full-suite verification (AH-0MVSE7ILL000Y27B) | task | AC1–AC7 evidence, seed sweep, gym↔game parity, full suite |

The dominant work is therefore authored data (`src/waves/Formations.ts`), not the sequencer. The sequencer still needs the distinctness constraint because AC1 binds on generated waves too.

- **Dominance, not purity:** D1 of the risk register (identity vs distinctness) is resolved by asserting dominant archetype + ≥ 2 archetypes per level + no adjacent duplicates — never "all ten waves distinct archetypes".
- **Rules win over distinctness:** R1–R3 keep precedence, matching the existing precedence in AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP; a wave that cannot meet distinctness inside the acceptance band becomes authored `fixed` data instead of widening the band.
- **No public API break:** `buildSequencedLevels(rows, candidates)` keeps working; the new controls are optional fields.

Each phase is a vertical slice, not a horizontal layer:

- **Phase A** delivers, in one green increment: the shared analysis code, its unit tests, the identity-pin contract, the authored Level 1/Level 5 data, the palette of comments and the audit report — proving the pattern end-to-end on the two hardest levels.
- **Phase B** delivers the generated-wave constraint plus the remaining authored data plus the mode ledger, each with its own tests and comments, keeping the whole campaign green at each step.

Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated with what the previous phase learned (recorded as comments on the parent). No phase is a horizontal "all tests then all code" split.

When a ship is destroyed and it has >=10 minerals to drop it should drop a red mineral deposit. When these are collected they the player gains 10 minerals. If a UFO collects them then any quantity over the UFO's capacity is lost.

## Current behaviour (verified in the repo)

- The kill-drop rule lives once in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`
  (`resolveMineralKillDrops`) and is consumed by `PlayScene` and
  `GymFormationScene`, so the game and every formation gym drop identically.
- A non-asteroid ship re-drops `mineralRedropCount(rng)` minerals — its absorbed
  count plus a random additive bonus (`mineralRedropBonusMin`/`Max`, defaults
  0.25/1.25, rounded) — scattered as **individual gold dots** within
  `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` (40 px) of the wreck. There is no upper cap.
- Each ordinary mineral is worth exactly 1: the player pickup path
  (`PlayScene._collectMineral` → `GameState.addMinerals(rules.mineralCollectAmount)`)
  and enemy absorption (`BaseEnemy.collectMineral`) both add 1 per dot.
- `Mineral` (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`) already carries a cosmetic `color`
  (`MINERAL_COLOR` gold, `MINERAL_SALVAGE_COLOR` orange) but **no value**; colour
  never changes worth.
- The friendly **Mystery UFO** collector drone (`src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts`,
  driven by the shared `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` pass) vacuums minerals
  inside its collector radius **up to its remaining capacity** and simply stops —
  minerals beyond capacity stay on the field. Its hold capacity is 10 → 20
  (`mysteryUfoCapacity`).
- Collection/absorption runs once in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`
  (`collectMinerals`); the player pickup callback receives the collected
  `Mineral`, so a per-mineral value can travel through the existing seam.
- The **Salvage** bounty scatters its level-resolved bonus as orange minerals in a
  *separate* call right after the kill seam (`PlayScene` ~line 3623,
  `GymFormationScene` ~line 1981, both via `scatterSalvageMineralDrops`); the count
  comes from `EffectsRegistry.salvageBonusMinerals()`.

## Desired behaviour

- A destroyed **ship** whose resolved drop count is **≥ 10** leaves a single
  **red mineral deposit** at the wreck; the deposit replaces the **entire** payout,
  so any value above 10 is lost (a wreck resolving 17 pays one 10-value deposit).
- Collecting a deposit pays the player **10 minerals in one pickup**.
- A hostile mineral-absorbing enemy that overlaps a deposit absorbs it as worth
  **10** (so its own later re-drop resolves at ≥10 and itself becomes a deposit).
- When the friendly UFO vacuums a deposit, it credits at most its **remaining
  capacity**; the surplus is lost (not left on the field, not paid out later).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Deposit at the resolved-count threshold.** When a destroyed ship's resolved mineral drop count — `mineralRedropCount(rng)`, i.e. absorbed minerals **plus** the random additive bonus, rounded — is **≥ `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_THRESHOLD` (10)**, the shared kill seam spawns exactly **one red mineral deposit** at the wreck and **no** individual gold minerals. A resolved count of **9 or less** keeps today's behaviour exactly. Covered in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts`: 9 → nine gold minerals; 10 → one deposit, zero gold minerals; and a colour assertion against the named deposit colour constant.
2. **Surplus above 10 is intentionally lost.** A wreck resolving 17 leaves exactly **one** deposit worth 10 and nothing else — no remainder gold minerals and no second deposit. Covered alongside AC 1 in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts`.
3. **Player pickup pays 10.** Overlapping the player ship with a live deposit collects it and adds exactly **`MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE` (10)** minerals to the run hold in a single pickup (one hold addition and one HUD update), independent of `mineralCollectAmount` (still 1 for an ordinary mineral). Covered in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.test.ts` and the `PlayScene` mineral tests.
4. **Deposit obeys the ordinary mineral rules.** A deposit is stationary, persists until collected, is never destroyed by bullets, causes no damage or collision response, is gated by the Phase-Shift collection gate during combat, and is attracted by Mineral Scoop/Magnet exactly like an ordinary mineral.
5. **Hostile enemies absorb a deposit as 10.** A non-asteroid enemy that overlaps a live deposit absorbs it worth **10** (equivalent to ten single-mineral absorptions), so its own later re-drop resolves at ≥ 10 and therefore pays out as a deposit. Asteroids stay inert to minerals (including deposits). Covered in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.test.ts` and the `BaseEnemy` mineral tests.
6. **UFO overflow is lost.** When the Mystery UFO collector drone vacuums a deposit, its hold grows by **at most its remaining capacity**; the surplus value is destroyed with the deposit — it is never left on the field, never paid into the hold and never credited to another entity. Covered in `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.test.ts` (partial-capacity and at-capacity cases).
7. **Salvage folds into one payout.** While the Salvage window is active its level-resolved bonus **counts toward** the ≥ 10 threshold; when the threshold fires the wreck pays **only** the red deposit and **no** orange Salvage scatter. Below the threshold, the ordinary gold drops **plus** the orange Salvage scatter are unchanged. Covered in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`.
8. **Single shared implementation (gym↔game parity).** The deposit spawn rule, the player pickup value, the valued enemy absorption and the drone overflow rule each exist exactly **once** in the shared seam (`src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`, `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`, `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts`) and are consumed by both `PlayScene` and the formation gyms; no scene-local copy is introduced, and the repo-wide defined-once guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` still passes.
9. **Constants and docs.** The threshold (10), value (10) and red colour are named constants in `src/core/constants.ts` beside `MINERAL_COLOR` — **no** `src/core/rules.ts` tunable and **no** persisted-rules schema migration. `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.5 (Minerals) documents the deposit: threshold basis, whole-payout replacement, player value, enemy absorption, UFO overflow and the shared seam it runs through.

## Decisions (producer answers, 2026-10-28)

All five questions below were answered by the producer with the recommended
option — the operator replied **"All questions as suggested"** to the comment
carrying these questions (`AH-0MVJ79739008396I`).

1. **Threshold basis → post-bonus resolved re-drop count.** The threshold compares against `mineralRedropCount(rng)` (absorbed + random additive bonus, rounded) — exactly the number of dots the wreck would have paid before this change.
2. **Surplus above 10 → lost.** The single deposit replaces the whole payout; value above 10 is an intentional sink.
3. **Collectors → UFO only for overflow; hostile enemies absorb a deposit as 10.** Overflow loss applies to the friendly Mystery UFO drone. Hostile non-asteroid enemies absorb a deposit worth 10 and re-drop accordingly.
4. **Tunables → fixed constants** in `src/core/constants.ts` (no `rules.ts` change, no schema migration).
5. **Salvage → counts toward the threshold, single payout.** The Salvage bonus is included in the resolved count; when the deposit fires the orange Salvage scatter is suppressed for that wreck, so one wreck always produces exactly one payout shape.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — single kill-drop seam; threshold decision, whole-payout replacement and Salvage suppression belong here.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — `collectMinerals`; player pickup value and valued enemy absorption.
- `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` — shared drone tick/vacuum wrapper (overflow accounting).
- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` — collectable entity; gains a value and the deposit colour.
- `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts` — drone vacuum + capacity accounting.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `mineralRedropCount` (threshold input) and valued absorption.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `MINERAL_COLOR`/`MINERAL_SIZE`; add `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_COLOR`, `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_THRESHOLD`, `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `salvageBonusMinerals()` (folded into the resolved count).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_collectMineral`, kill seam + Salvage scatter call site.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — gym kill seam + Salvage scatter call site (parity).
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.test.ts`, `src/entities/__tests__/Mineral.test.ts`, `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts`, `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 Minerals documentation.

## Assumptions

- "Ship" means a destroyed **non-asteroid** enemy ship (asteroid drops are unchanged: a small asteroid still drops one gold mineral).
- A deposit is a **mineral** for all existing mineral rules (persistence, no damage, bullet pass-through, phase gate, magnet/scoop attraction) — only its colour and worth differ.
- Because the deposit replaces the scatter at ≥ 10, the existing two-RNG-draws-per-dot scatter order no longer applies at those wrecks: a deterministic seeded-run capture will differ at them (expected, not a regression).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Session:** `herdr-1793209415-1968187-5973` (downtime-dispatched `/skill:plan`, resumed after producer answers).
- **Seed:** intake description only (no PRD, no linked design doc). No duplicate work found: `wl search "mineral deposit"` and `wl search "10x mineral"` returned only unrelated mineral/harvesting items; no existing "deposit" feature exists in the codebase (confirmed by grep for "deposit"/"MINERAL_RED").
- **Decision record:** `/skill:plan` pre-check returned `decision: "skip"` (effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low**), so the session ran the six automated review stages against the existing intake description instead of a full feature decomposition; no child work items were created.
- **Q1 (threshold basis):** Asked — "Is the ≥10 threshold the post-bonus resolved re-drop count or the absorbed count?" Answer (producer): *as suggested* → **post-bonus resolved re-drop count** (`mineralRedropCount`). Evidence: `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` `mineralRedropCount`, `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`. Final: resolved count.
- **Q2 (surplus above 10):** Asked — "Does one deposit replace all of a 17-mineral payout (7 lost) or 10 of it?" Answer (producer): *as suggested* → **replaces the whole payout; surplus lost**. Final: whole-payout replacement.
- **Q3 (which collectors):** Asked — "UFO only? Do hostile enemies absorb a deposit as 10 or ignore it?" Answer (producer): *as suggested* → **UFO only for overflow; hostile enemies absorb a deposit as 10**. Final: as stated (AC 5/AC 6).
- **Q4 (tunables):** Asked — "`rules.ts` tunables or fixed `constants.ts` constants?" Answer (producer): *as suggested* → **fixed constants in `src/core/constants.ts`**. Final: constants, no schema migration.
- **Q5 (Salvage interaction):** Asked — "Does the Salvage bonus count toward the threshold, and can both payouts appear at one wreck?" Answer (producer): *as suggested* → **bonus counts toward the threshold and only the deposit appears**. Final: single payout per wreck (AC 7).
- **Prior answers:** none — the questions were first raised in this planning session; no answer was revised.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 — `/skill:plan` (auto-plan decision `skip`: effort Extra Small, risk Low) ran the six automated review stages on the existing intake description. Added: issue type `feature`, `## Current behaviour`, `## Desired behaviour`, `## Acceptance Criteria` (6 ACs), `## Open Questions` (5), `## Key Files`, `## Assumptions`, `## Appendix`. No child work items created; AC coverage review returned `proceed`. Item marked needs-producer-review pending answers to OPEN QUESTIONS 1–5.
- 2026-10-28 — Producer answered all five questions with the recommended option ("All questions as suggested"). `## Open Questions` replaced by `## Decisions`; ACs expanded from 6 to 9 (added whole-payout surplus loss, hostile-enemy absorption worth 10, Salvage folding, and the constants/docs split); Appendix records each Q&A. AC coverage review re-run → `proceed`; needs-producer-review cleared.

# Intake brief — Full-suite runs dirty the main checkout ship-config.csv

> **Source request (verbatim):** "Full-suite test runs (observed with
> changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leave
> src/data/ship-config.csv modified in the MAIN checkout
> (thrustAcceleration/maxSpeed/frictionDeceleration/controlScheme changes),
> even though the suite runs from a worktree. A test exercising
> GymPlayer.saveShipConfig writes through the dev-server CSV plugin whose root
> resolves to the main checkout (likely via the symlinked node_modules / vite
> project root). This trips the implement dirty-tree gate on later sessions,
> requiring a git checkout restore; it can also silently clobber an operator's
> tuned ship config. … add a guard so suites never write the repo's tracked
> CSV."

## Headline

Full-suite test runs leak writes to the tracked `src/data/ship-config.csv` in the **main checkout** even when the suite runs from a worktree, breaking the implement dirty-tree gate and risking silent clobbering of an operator-tuned ship config. Fix the dev-server CSV plugin's root resolution and add a guard so suites never write a tracked repository CSV.

## Problem statement

Running the full test suite (observed during changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leaves `src/data/ship-config.csv` modified in the MAIN checkout — `thrustAcceleration`/`maxSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration`/`controlScheme` diverge from the committed values — despite the suite having run from a worktree. The only writer of the tracked CSVs is the dev-server CSV plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`): its write handler resolves `resolve(root, 'src/data/ship-config.csv')` where `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274), and the config store's dev-mode save (`saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves`, gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV`, which is `true` under vitest) issues a **relative** `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (`src/core/configStore.ts` lines 397–405, 569–586). In vitest's happy-dom integration project (default `window.location` = `http://localhost:3000`, verified in the installed vitest source), happy-dom's fetch resolves relative URLs against that origin — so a real (un-mocked) save PUTs to `http://localhost:3000/api/csv/...`; whatever server answers there can write through a root that points at the main checkout. Worktrees symlink `node_modules` to the main checkout (confirmed on four live worktrees), which lets Vite's project-root/package-root inference escape to the main checkout. The worktree's own `csv-seed.test.ts` reads its CSVs via `__dirname`, so a leaked write to the *other* checkout is not caught by the seed tests in the active checkout. Consequences: the implement dirty-tree gate fails on later sessions (manual `git checkout` restore required), and an operator-tuned ship config can be silently clobbered; it likely also explains intermittent `csv-seed` / `<suite exited 1>` smoke failures (AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL, AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP, AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2).

## Users

- **Developers / AI agents running the suite** — "As a developer I want suite runs to never modify tracked config files in any checkout, so the implement dirty-tree gate stays green and I don't have to restore files manually."
- **Designers/operators tuning ship config** — "As a designer I want my tuned `ship-config.csv` to survive test runs, so my balance work isn't silently overwritten."
- **Test suite maintainers** — "As a test author I want tests to exercise save behaviour against isolated fixtures, so the suite is deterministic and hermetic."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No tracked-file writes from suites** — Running the audit-accepted full suite (`npm --silent test`: `unit` + `integration` projects) from a worktree leaves every tracked `src/data/*.csv` (`ship-config.csv`, `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`) unchanged in **both** the active worktree and the main checkout. Verified by an automated pre/post `git status --porcelain` of both checkouts that runs as part of the change's tests (a regression guard the suite itself asserts).
2. **Root isolation in the plugin** — The CSV plugin never resolves write targets to a checkout other than the active project root: the implicit `process.cwd()` default is replaced by an explicit, verified root (derived from the Vite-resolved root, or an explicit option), and any request whose resolved target escapes the active root is refused with no file I/O (HTTP error + logged reason). Existing explicit-root test fixtures keep working unchanged.
3. **Test-mode write guard in the store** — Under the vitest/test harness (`import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'` detected in `configStore.ts`), `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` must never write a tracked repository file: they either update the registry only (documented no-op wrt disk, preserving registry semantics used by tests) or route writes to an isolated temp fixture. A direct unit test covers each save function under test mode asserting no file on disk changes.
4. **Escape route closed** — No test can PUT through a live dev-server endpoint by accident: relative `/api/csv/...` fetches in the happy-dom project must resolve against a test-controlled origin (explicit bridge/stub), never a stray `localhost` server that could answer from the main checkout. Add a comment in the integration tests documenting the relative-fetch/bridge pattern and verifying the bridge is installed for every real save.
5. **Documentation and full suite** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (plugin root semantics, test-mode guard and store save behaviour) and any relevant wiki/docs entries. The full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and the existing seed/validation tests (`csv-seed.test.ts`, `configStore.*`, plugin tests, gym save tests) remain green.

## Constraints

- Dev-only behaviour is preserved: while `npm run dev` runs from the active checkout, gym Save/Save As must still persist through the plugin to the committed CSVs (read-write dev workflow, AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA). Production builds stay read-only (`apply: 'serve'`).
- Atomic-write semantics (temp file + rename) and the post-save registry re-read (`reReadRegistry`) must be preserved on the success path.
- Test isolation is a requirement, not an option: current unit/integration tests already pin temp fixtures via explicit `root`; the gap is the default path and the dev-mode relative fetch. Do not weaken existing fixture patterns.
- Worktree isolation rules apply: implementation happens in a worktree; the main checkout is never edited directly.
- UK English for prose/comments; Markdown for work-item and code-doc prose.

## Existing state

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — `configCsvPlugin(options)`: `const root = options.root ?? process.cwd();` (line 274); `handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath), …)` for ship/enemy/difficulty CSVs. Registered in `vite.config.ts` with no options (`configCsvPlugin()`, so default root = `process.cwd()` of the dev server / test process).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isDev()` = `import.meta.env.DEV === true` (line 97); `fetchCsv`/`putCsv` use relative `/api/csv/...` URLs (lines 397–405, 569–586); `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` (lines ~612–660) gate only on `isDev()`.
- Vitest config (`vitest.config.ts`) — `unit` (node) and `integration` (happy-dom, default origin `http://localhost:3000`) projects; `isolate: true`; the full suite is `unit` + `integration`.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` (lines 80, 121–133) and `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — real plugin behind an ephemeral HTTP server against a **temp** root with an explicit fetch bridge; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts` / `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — `vi.mock('../../core/configStore')` replacing `saveShipConfig` with an in-process registry seed; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — reads CSVs via `__dirname`, i.e. relative to the **active** checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it.
- Worktree layout — `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with `node_modules` symlinked to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed on four live worktrees: wl-AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40-*, wl-AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V-*, wl-AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q-*, wl-AH-0MVNT27XR0080I3C-*).

## Desired change

1. Make the plugin's write root explicit and safe: derive it from the Vite server's resolved project root (with an explicit override option), and refuse any write whose target resolves outside the active root. This removes the unpredictable `process.cwd()` default.
2. Add a store-level test-mode guard so the vitest harness can never write tracked files (registry-only no-op or temp-fixture routing), closing the relative-fetch escape route at the source.
3. Harden regression coverage: a suite-run cleanliness assertion (pre/post `git status` on both checkouts) plus unit tests for the new root guard and the test-mode guard.
4. Document the safe patterns (explicit roots, fetch bridges, module mocks) alongside the plugin and store modules.

## Key Files

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — replace the `process.cwd()` default root with an explicit/Vite-resolved root that is verified against the active checkout; add the escape-refusal guard; update `ConfigCsvPluginOptions` docs.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — tests for default-root behaviour (must not write outside active root) and the escape-refusal guard.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — add test-mode detection to `isDev()`/save guards; document relative-fetch + bridge pattern.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` / `configStore.integration.test.ts` — tests for test-mode save no-op/temp routing; fixture pattern comments.
- `vite.config.ts` — pass an explicit root derived from `server.config.root` if the plugin cannot self-derive it.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — optionally extend the seed check to also assert a clean worktree/main-checkout diff (the suite-run cleanliness guard may live here or in a new small test).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` (only if behaviour changes; otherwise untouched) — `_onSave` consumes `saveShipConfig`'s `ok/reason`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole": where the leak was first observed (`discovered-from`).
- **AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL** — "[test-failure] csv-seed.test.ts / configStore.integration.test.ts — ship-config.csv diverges from DEFAULT_CONFIG": the smoke symptom of a leaked write (`thrustAcceleration 390` vs `300`).
- **AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT** — "enemy-configs.csv working-tree change removes header and trailing newline (fails csv-seed tests)": sibling symptom on the enemy CSV.
- **AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP**, **AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2** — "[test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test": possibly same intermittent root cause.
- **AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA** (config-store epic), **AH-0MUE2MHRC0090AXP** (CSV plugin), **AH-0MUE2MIK9001TK88** (integration tests) — origin of the dev write-back design being hardened here.
- **AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V** — "Ship config controlScheme does not survive game server restart": dev-server persistence semantics for ship config.
- **AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4** — "Gym config save strips the CSV comment header block": another save-path quirk.
- **AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM** (open) — "Dev-mode write-back: gym Save to repo persists bot tuning": the same "dev writes to tracked repo data" family; keep separate.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-broad guard breaks the legit dev save flow** — mitigation: scope the refusal to (a) targets outside the active root and (b) test-mode; the dev-mode save path from the active checkout must keep working (AC2 keeps explicit-root fixtures valid).
- **Stray server on the happy-dom origin (localhost:3000) still receives writes if only the plugin changes** — the store-level test-mode guard (AC3) is the belt-and-braces fix; do not rely on the plugin alone.
- **Root-cause mechanism partially inferred** — the exact process that answers the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run was not reproduced deterministically in this intake; the implementer must reproduce and confirm before finalising the guard wording (record the reproduction in the work item). Non-blocking for the fix: ACs are observable-outcome based.
- **Scope creep** — protecting against an operator's accidental save overwriting a tuned config in the *browser/UI* (e.g. a confirmation prompt) is a separate UX concern; record it as a separate item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption** — `npm --silent test` remains the audit-accepted full suite; suite runs from implement worktrees use symlinked node_modules; vitest happy-dom default origin is `http://localhost:3000` and happy-dom resolves relative fetches against it (verified in installed `vitest`/`happy-dom` sources at intake time).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed context (title + description of AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) already contained the observed symptom, the primary hypothesis (root resolution via symlinked node_modules / vite project root), and the suggested fix directions. Research performed during intake:

- **Q (self): "Which code path is the only writer of the tracked CSVs?"** — Answer (Map): `configCsvPlugin.handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath))` in `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`; `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274). Source: code inspection of `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, `vite.config.ts` (plugin registered without options).
- **Q (self): "How does a suite-run write escape the temp-fixture pattern?"** — Answer (Map): all plugin instantiations in tests pass explicit temp roots (`configCsvPlugin.test.ts` line 100/447, `configStore.integration.test.ts` line 80) and GymPlayer tests mock the store — so the leak is not from these; the store's dev-mode save issues a relative `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (configStore.ts lines 397–405, 569–586) gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV` (true under vitest). In the happy-dom integration project, happy-dom's `Fetch` resolves the relative URL against `window.location.href` (verified in `node_modules/happy-dom/lib/fetch/Fetch.js`), whose vitest default is `http://localhost:3000` (verified in `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DC7d2Pf8.js` line 343). A real server on that origin with a root at the main checkout receives the PUT.
- **Q (self): "Why does the worktree's root resolve to the main checkout?"** — Answer (Map): worktree `node_modules` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed via `ls -la` on four live worktrees), so Vite's package-root/workspace-root detection and any module-relative path resolution can escape to the main checkout. Likely, not yet reproduced end-to-end (recorded in Risks).
- **Q (self): "Why doesn't the active checkout's csv-seed test catch the leak?"** — Answer (Map): `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` reads CSVs via `resolve(__dirname, …)`, i.e. the active checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it. Source: code inspection.
- **Q (self): "Are there existing related items?"** — Answer (Map): yes — AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL (ship-config smoke failure), AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT (enemy-config analogue), AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP / AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2 (generic suite-exit-1), AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V, AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4, AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM. Source: `wl search` during intake step 2.
- **Open question for the implementer (not a producer blocker):** reproduce the exact answering server/process on the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run and record it; the ACs are outcome-verifiable regardless.

# Net-new unlock-pool weapon feel package + catalogue-wide fire/impact guard

**discovered-from:AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW** (5 net-new weapon types) — an audit of the `shard_swarm` player weapon found it shipped with an in-flight bullet look only: no fire sound, no muzzle flash and no per-weapon impact feedback. Widening that audit to the whole catalogue (producer decision Q2 = B, see the Appendix) found the gap is **systemic across all five net-new unlock-pool weapons** and that nothing mechanically prevents a new weapon from shipping with no feel package.

## Problem statement

Two findings drive this item:

1. **`shard_swarm` (the original audit).** The weapon has a bespoke lime `shard` fan silhouette and no feel package at all: it fires silently, shows no launch cue at the ship, and every connect produces only the generic warm-white impact flash with no hit sound. Against the neon field its 0.72× lime shards read as weak visual noise, so the "shotgun burst" identity its ±15° fan is designed to deliver never reaches the player's ears or eye.
2. **The gap is catalogue-wide and unguarded (Q2 = B).** Measured state: **no** net-new unlock-pool weapon has a `playWeaponFireSound` case, **none** declares `muzzleFlash`, and **none** declares `impactFx`. The 11 original weapons all have the package; nothing in the test suite asserts the package exists, so the five new weapons shipped without it and the next weapon can too.

| Weapon | Colour | Shape | Fire cue | `muzzleFlash` | `impactFx` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11 original weapons | — | — | ✔ all | ✔ all | ✔ 9/11 (`nova`/`mortar` use the AOE seam by design) |
| `rear_guard` | rose `0xff5599` | `pellet` | ✘ | ✘ | ✘ |
| `broadside` | teal `0x44ffdd` | `dart` | ✘ | ✘ | ✘ |
| `railgun` | sky `0x66aaff` | `tracer` | ✘ (planned: AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA) | ✘ (planned: AH-0MVQ6C1YL003HU9K) | ✘ (planned: AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA) |
| `shard_swarm` | lime `0xc0ff33` | `shard` | ✘ | ✘ | ✘ |
| `heavy_slug` | red `0xff2222` | `heavy-shell` | ✘ | ✘ | ✘ |

## Users and outcomes

**Primary user:** the player who unlocked a mini-boss reward weapon (all five are mini-boss unlock-pool weapons, GDD §4.4.4).

- As a player firing a Shard Swarm, I want an audible launch and a lime shard-coloured hit so I can hear the fan leave the ship and hear it connect.
- As a player holding any unlock-pool weapon, I want its launch and hit to be audible and colour-matched to its projectile, so a weapon I only obtained after a mini-boss fight does not feel unfinished next to the starting eleven.
- As a player flying through a dense wave, I want each weapon's projectiles (and the Diver's shards) to stay readable against the neon field, not merge into a blur at high upgrade levels.
- As a developer adding a 17th weapon, I want the build to **fail** if I forget the fire cue, the launch flash or the impact feedback, instead of shipping a silent weapon.
- As a player at the hold-full overlay, I want the reduced-volume metronome to include these weapons, so the beat keeps sounding while I choose.

## Current state (verified against source)

Shared seams that already exist and are consumed identically by the game and every gym:

- **Fire dispatch:** `playWeaponFireSound(weaponId, options)` (`src/audio/effects.ts:683`) — one switch, 11 cases, `default:` no-op. Every net-new weapon id falls through to the no-op, so live fire, the hold-full metronome (`HOLD_FULL_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`) and gym fire are all silent.
- **Launch cue:** `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` spawns the muzzle flash only `if (def.muzzleFlash)`; `MuzzleFlashSpec` is `{ color, radius, duration }` (`src/utils/weapons.ts:833`).
- **Impact feedback:** `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:508`) no-ops without `impactFx`; `damageEnemyWithBullet` then falls back to the generic warm-white `spawnBulletImpact(…, 0xfff2a0, r7)`. Impact cues dispatch through `playWeaponImpactCue` → `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES` (`src/audio/effects.ts:541`, 9 entries).
- **In-flight drawing:** `resolvePlayerBulletVisual` / `resolveEnemyBulletVisual` in `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` are the single source for player and enemy projectiles; the `shard` primitive `_shard` (`bulletVisuals.ts:537`) draws **both** the player's `shard_swarm` bullets and the Diver enemy's spread-burst projectile (AH-0MV822D2U000LRFV), with a hardcoded white spine/glint and a metadata-driven rim.
- **Level resolution:** `resolveWeaponDefinition` already carries visual metadata through levelling — pinned by `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts` (`muzzleFlash`/`impactFx` equal to base at levels). **No production change needed in `weaponLevels.ts`.**
- **Density guard:** the per-cue voice limiter (`MAX_CONCURRENT_CUE_VOICES = 4`, `CUE_VOICE_WINDOW_MS = 150`, `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts`) bounds overlapping voices per cue, so a five-shard volley (or a Heavy Slug fired into a crowd) cannot stack unboundedly.
- **Gyms exercising these weapons:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts:112`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts:93` (both list all five ids); the Diver appears in `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts`.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want every unlock-pool weapon to sound and read like the weapon its silhouette promises — an audible, colour-matched launch and hit plus a legible projectile — and as a maintainer I want the build to refuse a weapon that ships without that feel package, so the Shard Swarm's missing feedback can never be repeated by the next weapon.

## Desired change

Per-weapon feel package (metadata + two baked cues each; railgun supplied by its existing planned items — see *Scope decisions*):

| Weapon | Fire cue (new) | Impact cue (new) | `muzzleFlash` | `impactFx` | Character sketch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shard_swarm` | `playShardSwarmFireSound` / `aihell-shard-swarm-fire` | `playShardSwarmImpactSound` / `aihell-shard-swarm-impact` | lime, sized for a five-shard burst | lime family, short | tight multi-shard "chk" burst; bright glassy lime tink ≤0.12 s |
| `rear_guard` | `playRearGuardFireSound` / `aihell-rear-guard-fire` | `playRearGuardImpactSound` / `aihell-rear-guard-impact` | rose, compact | rose family | muted rearward "thup", darker than the Cannon's forward thump; soft rose pop |
| `broadside` | `playBroadsideFireSound` / `aihell-broadside-fire` | `playBroadsideImpactSound` / `aihell-broadside-impact` | teal, wide pair | teal family | wide two-sided swish (reads as left+right leaving the hull); short teal dart tick |
| `heavy_slug` | `playHeavySlugFireSound` / `aihell-heavy-slug-fire` | `playHeavySlugImpactSound` / `aihell-heavy-slug-impact` | deep red, largest of the set | deep red, largest radius of the set | heavy low boom + metallic clank; dull red thud with debris noise |
| `railgun` | *planned by AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA* | *planned by AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA* | *planned by AH-0MVQ6C1YL003HU9K* | *planned by AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA* | — (no duplicate work here) |

Plus:

- **In-flight legibility via the shared `shard` primitive (Q1 = C).** Strengthen `_shard` itself so the shard silhouette reads harder against the neon field — stronger spine/rim contrast and a more visible glint. This intentionally applies to **both** the player's shards and the Diver's enemy shards, and the Diver's documented identity (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, roster row + §E2 narrative) is updated to match.
- **A catalogue-wide feel guard (Q2 = B).** A mechanical guard over `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` assert, for every weapon id: a `playWeaponFireSound` case that dispatches a manifest-mapped cue; a declared `muzzleFlash`; and impact feedback — either a declared `impactFx` with a manifest-mapped cue, or (for the AOE family) a documented AOE impact/detonation cue. The guard's purpose is to make the next silent weapon a build failure, not a player complaint.

## Scope decisions (from producer answers)

- **Q1 = C** — strengthen `_shard` for every consumer (player shards *and* the Diver enemy attack). Restyling the Diver's projectile is accepted and deliberate; the Diver's documented visual identity is updated in the same change so docs and code cannot drift. The roster **signature** values (shape/colour/length/rim/thickness) are unchanged, so the uniqueness guards stay green.
- **Q2 = B** — add the catalogue-wide guard now and complete the feel package for the three untracked siblings (`rear_guard`, `broadside`, `heavy_slug`) **inside this item**.
- **Railgun is not re-implemented here.** Its fire and impact SFX are already specified and planned at `plan_complete` by Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA), and its muzzle flash by Railgun launch muzzle-flash VFX (AH-0MVQ6C1YL003HU9K). Duplicating that planned work would waste an approved plan and risk two divergent cue designs, so this item takes **dependency edges** on both and the catalogue-wide guard turns green only once they land. If the producer prefers the railgun work to be absorbed here instead, the two railgun items should be closed as superseded first (closing requires producer approval).
- **No behaviour or balance change.** `fireRateMs`, `offsets`, `bulletLifetime`, `bulletSize`, `bulletShape(Length)`, `bulletSpeed`, `bulletColor` and `maxHitPoints` stay exactly as they are for all five weapons. Legibility changes touch only the drawing of the shared `shard` primitive (Q1 = C).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Catalogue-wide feel guard.** A new test (audio/roster layer) asserts, for **all 16** catalogue weapon ids: (a) `playWeaponFireSound(id)` dispatches a cue that exists in `CUE_MANIFEST`; (b) the definition declares `muzzleFlash` with a weapon-family colour; (c) impact feedback is declared — an `impactFx` whose `cue` is in `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`, or, for the AOE family (`nova`, `mortar`), a documented AOE impact/detonation cue. The guard fails today for the five net-new weapons and passes when this item (plus the two railgun items) is done.
- **AC2 — `shard_swarm` feel.** New `playShardSwarmFireSound` and `playShardSwarmImpactSound` (recipes `aihell-shard-swarm-fire`, `aihell-shard-swarm-impact`); `playWeaponFireSound('shard_swarm')` routes to the fire cue, `impactFx` (`color` = lime family, `radius`, `duration`, `cue: 'playShardSwarmImpactSound'`) is declared and registered in `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`, and `muzzleFlash` (lime, sized for a five-shard burst) spawns through the shared `_autoFire` → `spawnMuzzleFlash` path. The generic white fallback flash no longer applies to this weapon.
- **AC3 — `rear_guard` feel.** Same package (rose family) with `aihell-rear-guard-fire` / `aihell-rear-guard-impact`; the cues are audibly distinct from the Cannon's (rearward, darker, more muffled) so the backward shot is identifiable by ear.
- **AC4 — `broadside` feel.** Same package (teal family) with `aihell-broadside-fire` / `aihell-broadside-impact`; the fire cue reads as a wide two-sided launch pair rather than a second Cannon.
- **AC5 — `heavy_slug` feel.** Same package (deep-red family, the largest flash radius and lowest-pitched cue of the set) with `aihell-heavy-slug-fire` / `aihell-heavy-slug-impact`; the cue is the game's heaviest single-shot fire sound without aliasing the Mortar detonation.
- **AC6 — Railgun covered, not duplicated.** `railgun` satisfies AC1 through AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA and AH-0MVQ6C1YL003HU9K (dependency edges recorded); this item introduces no railgun cue, recipe or metadata.
- **AC7 — Stronger `shard` primitive (player + Diver).** `_shard` renders a higher-contrast spine/rim and a more visible glint; both `shard_swarm` player bullets and the Diver enemy shards are drawn by the unchanged single seam (no per-scene copy, no new primitive). The roster **signature** for both consumers is unchanged (uniqueness guards stay green), while a dedicated test pins that the strengthened drawing is applied to both consumers.
- **AC8 — No density/legibility regressions.** At full upgrade levels the five-shard fan does not become a screen-filling blur: every new `muzzleFlash`/`impactFx` radius and duration stays within the shipped per-weapon range (radius ≤ the largest shipped value, duration ≤ 0.16 s), and the natural cadence plus the existing per-cue voice limiter (4 voices / 150 ms) bound the added audio load — no new throttling logic is added.
- **AC9 — Audio catalogue + docs updated.** `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` records all new cues in **both** tables (cue → disposition, recipe → seed), `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` lists each as `delivery: "baked"` with recorded seeds, `scripts/build-audio.sh --verify` passes, GDD §4.4 (net-new-weapon note and per-weapon rows) and §7.3 describe every weapon's fire/impact identity, and the README `src/utils/weapons.ts` / audio notes list the five weapons' fire and impact cues instead of leaving them as silhouette-only entries.
- **AC10 — Gym↔game parity.** Every change lands in the shared core/seams (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`, `src/vfx/`, `src/audio/`) and is consumed identically by `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymWeaponLeveling` (and the Diver's strengthened shard by whichever gym hosts the Diver); the duplicate-body guard, `CombatScene.equivalence` and the gym-parity/documentation roster guards pass unchanged.
- **AC11 — Testing/validation.** New or updated tests cover: the catalogue-wide feel guard; fire-cue dispatch for each new weapon; `impactFx` resolution and colour-matched flashes through `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx`; muzzle-flash spawn through the shared core; level-resolved metadata survival for each new weapon; the `_shard` draw for both consumers; the Diver documentation roster; and the audio contract (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts` / `cueManifest` coverage of every new cue). Audio must remain a safe no-op with no audio context.
- **AC12 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, the Diver's entry in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, and any relevant docs-site entries.
- **AC13 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes (run through the test skill, not ad-hoc).

## Constraints

- **Baked audio only.** ToneForge assets are baked, not runtime-synthesised (`src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` is the sole runtime exception): each new cue needs a recipe YAML under `audio/toneforge/recipes/`, a `manifest.json` entry with its seed(s) and a `scripts/build-audio.sh --render` run.
- **Headless safety.** Audio stays a safe no-op with no audio context.
- **Metadata-first.** No new hook in `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene` unless the metadata path proves insufficient; both seams already exist.
- **Naming convention.** `play<Weapon><Fire|Impact>Sound`, slug `aihell-<weapon>-<fire|impact>` — required because the contract test enumerates every `play*`/`update*`/`stop*` export and requires a manifest mapping.
- **One shared dispatcher, one switch.** No per-scene fire-cue switches; the metronome path must resolve the same cue as live fire.
- **AOE family exemption is explicit.** `nova`/`mortar` fire through the AOE seam (`onFire`/`onRandom`) and legitimately have no per-shot `impactFx`; the guard must encode that as an exemption with a reason, not a special case bolted on at the call site.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `muzzleFlash` / `impactFx` for `shard_swarm`, `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `heavy_slug`.

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC3: unmistakable warp transition timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS`; related to AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU "unmistakable" bar).

## Goal

As a player I want an unmistakable hyperspace "warp" when the background changes between levels, and as a developer I want that effect to be a deterministic, time-boxed, individually switchable module with a testable timeline, so level changes read as a jump through space without ever hurting readability or blocking play.

## Background

Producer answer Q2 (2026-10-25): **Option A — hyperspace-style one-shot** (converging streak overlay + radial scale distortion + brief flash/crossfade), timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s, currently exported from `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`). Existing VFX modules show the house pattern to copy: exported tuning constants plus per-layer `*_ENABLE_*` toggles and caller-owned effect registries that are destroyed on `SHUTDOWN` (`src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`, `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`).

Import direction matters: `PlayScene` imports VFX modules, so a VFX module must **not** import `PlayScene`. The duration therefore moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and is re-exported from `PlayScene` for existing importers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and `PlayScene` re-exports it unchanged, so `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` can derive `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` from the same single source (no duplicated literal); all existing importers (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`) keep compiling without edits.
2. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` exposes the full timeline as exported constants (streak phase, distortion/scale phase, flash/crossfade phase) whose phases are ordered, non-overlapping and sum to the total duration; a test asserts the sum and ordering so the effect can never outlive the transition window.
3. The effect renders three layers — converging streak overlay, radial scale distortion, brief flash/crossfade into the incoming background — each with its own `BACKGROUND_WARP_ENABLE_*` toggle (following the `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_*` pattern) and exported magnitudes (streak count, speed, colours, scale range, flash alpha).
4. Deterministic: no `Math.random()` (or a seeded generator) — two runs from the same inputs produce byte-identical layer parameters, asserted by test. Time-boxed and observable: an `update(dt)`-style tick API (no reliance on wall-clock tweens) so a test can advance exactly `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` and assert completion; `isComplete()` is true at the end and never before.
5. Bounded and disposable: a fixed maximum streak count (constant), all display objects inside one container, `destroy()` idempotent, and a test asserts the container/children are gone after completion and after an early `destroy()` (no leaks if the scene restarts mid-warp).
6. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` covers the ACs above; changed-scope tests and `tsc --noEmit` pass.

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #3 — "A "warp" transition effect plays while backgrounds change — timed to the existing `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s) transition pause — after which the new level's background is fully shown; the effect is deterministic, time-boxed, and does not block input or wave progression." — specifically the warp effect module itself (deterministic, time-boxed, switchable); the non-blocking wiring is AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write the test file first against the constant/API surface you intend to ship (red → green).
- Implement the effect as Phaser `Graphics` inside a `Container` at a depth just above the background layer and below gameplay (exported depth constant); no new assets and no new dependencies.
- Choose deterministic pseudo-randomness from a small in-module LCG seeded by `(fromLevel, toLevel)` so each level pair looks slightly different but reproducible — never `Math.random()`.
- Drive animation from an explicit `update(dt)`/`tick` call (the scene's `update` feeds it) rather than `this.tweens`, matching the deterministic-boot test harness in `src/test/gameHarness.ts`.
- Keep it visually consistent with `wormholeSpawn`/`phaseShiftJuice` (violet→cyan converging lines, white flash peak).
- Do not trigger it from a scene here — the wiring slice owns the trigger; this slice ships the module plus tests.

## Deliverables

- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` — deterministic, switchable hyperspace warp effect with exported timeline.
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` — timeline, determinism, completion, toggle and teardown tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` relocated (single source of truth).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — re-export only (no behaviour change).

**Key Files:**

- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` — new warp transition module.
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` — new tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` + warp depth/colour constants.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — re-export `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (no logic change).
- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` / `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — patterns to mirror (read-only).
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — visual-language reference (read-only).

## Dependencies

- Depends on: AH-0MVSEASIM005TU95 (deterministic background manifest — level identifiers/seeding only).
- Blocks: AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD (PlayScene level-change wiring).
- Related: AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU (unmistakable phase-shift/wormhole effects) — same producer bar, coordinate the visual language; this slice must not weaken that item's effect.
